construction.name: complete_triangular_strips_in_mixed_axis_layers
construction.proof:
ALTERNATING WHOLE-TRIANGLE STRIP RETURN

The ordinary bounding cell loses half its area for an equilateral triangle.
Recover that area by a physical marked return before attempting a metric
realization. Put a=1/sqrt(3). The canonical unit-edge triangle has vertices
(a,0),(-a/2,1/2),(-a/2,-1/2). For index t>=0, use its identity frame when
t is even and its half-turn about z when t is odd. Put its center at
((t mod 2)*a/2,t/2,0). Consecutive triangles share a complete oblique edge;
their interiors lie on opposite sides of that edge. Nonconsecutive
triangles have disjoint y interiors except possible shared boundary.
Extruding each complete triangle through the same prism height L keeps
the same nonoverlap and all whole-owner identities.

A strip of m such prisms lies in the exact rectangle
[-a/2,a] by [-1/2,m/2], extruded through [-L/2,L/2]. Its dimensions are
sqrt(3)/2, (m+1)/2, L. Its midpoint is (a/4,(m-1)/4,0).
The additional half-unit of height is the retained pair of end costs;
it may not be discarded by an infinite-strip density argument.

Put complete strips in disjoint rectangular grid cells using these exact
dimensions. A grid A by B by C fits in the common cube of side
max(A*sqrt(3)/2,B*(m+1)/2,C*L), and contains A*B*C*m complete prisms.
Keep an explicitly indexed subset of N whole owners. This is a complete
finite return, not a marginal planar capacity statement.

The source is the classical equilateral triangular tiling and Cartesian
composition. PingYou Ltd supplies the finite strip/grid assemblies and
their certificates, without claiming the classical tiling as new. The
zero-gain ordinary-length branch and every tested finite strip length
remain useful controls. Native witnesses round the prescribed centers,
apply one common tiny outward dilation, retain the exact two half-turn
quaternions, and are checked on every actual host wall and owner pair.

COMPLETE TRIANGULAR STRIPS IN MIXED-AXIS LAYERS

Use the complete m-owner source in TRIANGLE_STRIP_PROOF.txt as one module.
Its box dimensions are sqrt(3)/2, (m+1)/2, L; the half-unit end cost stays
in every copy. Apply only the identity and the two fixed cyclic coordinate
rotations. A layer whose vertical intrinsic dimension is dk contains a
rectangular grid of complete modules with the other two dimensions.

For a common transverse side S and layer word (L0,L1,L2), the number of
whole prism owners is m times the sum over k of
Lk*floor(S/di)*floor(S/dj), where {i,j,k}={0,1,2}. The actual total layer
height is L0*d0+L1*d1+L2*d2. The common enclosing cube has side the maximum
of S and this height. Layers are centered as one stack; the modules in
each layer share the same transverse cube walls. No layer or module has
an independent enclosing scale.

Every module's internal alternating owners and source frames are carried
through its common cyclic rotation. Between modules the complete boxes
separate; inside each module the marked whole-triangle return supplies
separation. Deleting a named owner is permitted only after retaining the
full parent module and the complete assembly decoder. All native centers
receive one common outward dilation, with a matching host dilation; every
actual owner pair and host wall is then checked exactly.
construction.native_decoder: Assemble cyclic layer types0,1,2 in order, centered as one full stack. Center each layer module-grid in x,y. For strip owner t use local point ((t mod2)*sqrt(3)/6-sqrt(3)/12,t/2-(m-1)/4,0), rotate it by the layer cyclic quaternion and add its module center. Owner quaternion is cyclic_quaternion*parity_quaternion[t mod2]. Retain the listed owner words and multiply all centers by1.0000001; inflate the common host by the same factor plus1e-7.
